questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India, consider the following statements:
1. Gujarat became the second State after Uttarakhand to pass a UCC Bill.
2. Article 44 in Part IV provides that the State shall endeavour to secure a UCC throughout India.
3. The 21st Law Commission (2018) held that a UCC was necessary and desirable at that stage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 21st Law Commission underlined that UCC is neither necessary nor desirable at this stage. Goa practises a form of common civil code under the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to judicial pronouncements related to the Uniform Civil Code, consider the following statements:
1. In Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum (1985) the Supreme Court directed Parliament to frame a law on UCC.
2. In Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017) the Court declared instant triple talaq unconstitutional.
3. In Jose Paulo Coutinho (2019) the Court cited the Goa Civil Code as a practical model of UCC.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In Sarla Mudgal (1995) the Court stressed the need for a UCC for gender equality, and in John Vellamettom (2003) it said UCC would help national integration.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides which one of the following?
opts: Marriage only between persons of the same religion
Registration of marriages only by religious bodies
Separate marriage laws for each linguistic group
questions.why: It gives an option outside religious personal laws. Hindu, Muslim, Christian and Parsi communities follow separate personal laws such as the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the food sector reforms from 1 April 2026, consider the following statements:
1. A Central licence is required for businesses with turnover above Rs 5 crore.
2. FSSAI registrations and licences are given perpetual validity, removing periodic renewals.
3. Businesses with annual turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore need only registration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: A State licence applies to turnover between Rs 1.5 crore and Rs 50 crore, and a Central licence applies above Rs 50 crore. The registration limit was raised from Rs 12 lakh.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), consider the following statements:
1. It is a statutory authority under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
2. Its administrative Ministry is the Ministry of Consumer Affairs.
3. The Act replaced eight earlier multi-departmental acts and orders, including the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The administrative Ministry is the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. FSSAI leads the Eat Right India movement and works on front-of-pack labelling.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of food in India, consider the following statements:
1. Street vendors registered under the Street Vendors Act, 2014 are treated as automatically registered with FSSAI.
2. Customs shall not clear imported food unless it has at least 60% of shelf life or three months before expiry, whichever is less.
3. The Parliamentary Committee found that only 2% of inspections reported non-compliance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. There are 266 laboratories in the country, and many lack facilities to test heavy metals, pesticides and bacteria.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It applies to CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB.
2. Assam Rifles and the NSG are not included at present.
3. All posts of Inspector General in these forces are to be filled by deputation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: 50% of IG posts are to be filled by deputation of IPS officers. At least 67% of Additional Director General posts and all posts of Director General and Special Director General are also filled by deputation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Consumer Justice Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The share of women among members of State Commissions rose from 29% to 35%.
2. It was released by the India Justice Report.
3. Case pendency rose by 21% between 2020 and 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The share declined from an average of 35% in 2021 to 29% in 2025. Only 134 cases were referred to mediation across 23 States, and nearly half of the State Commissions lacked a sitting president.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to postal ballots in India, consider the following statements:
1. The facility was extended to electors above 85 years and persons with disabilities.
2. Postal voting is governed by the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
3. The President and Governors are included among special voters.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Service voters include members of the armed forces and central armed police forces, and absentee voters include those under preventive detention.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Election Commission has made the Media Certification and Monitoring Committee (MCMC) responsible for pre-certification of political advertisements on electronic and social media.
Statement-II: The MCMC was created by the ECI to prevent paid news and misleading content.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct. The MCMC ensures compliance with the ECI guidelines and keeps a strict vigil on suspected paid news.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Sujal Gaon ID launched by the Ministry of Jal Shakti is which one of the following?
opts: Digital ID for rural piped water schemes
A tax identity number for water utilities
An identity card for village water committees
A rating scale for groundwater quality
questions.why: It enables source-to-tap mapping under the Jal Jeevan Mission and is linked to the Sujalam Bharat digital architecture. It supports Har Ghar Jal coverage by 2028.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the US-Iran war, consider the following statements:
1. The US and Israel launched coordinated strikes called Operation Epic Fury.
2. Iran did not retaliate against any US or Gulf targets.
3. The strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Iran retaliated against US military facilities in the region, Israel, and energy and civilian infrastructure in the Gulf states. Brent crude went past $110 per barrel after strikes on Kharg Island and South Pars.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the costs of the West Asia conflict, consider the following statements:
1. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz caused global port congestion.
2. Rising costs risk pushing 8.8 million people across 14 countries into poverty.
3. Middle East shipping insurance fell by 50%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Shipping insurance in the Middle East spiked by 50%. Iran suffers the sharpest HDI decline, losing 1 to 1.5 years of human development.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the impact of the West Asia conflict on India, consider the following statements:
1. About half of India's crude oil imports transit the Strait of Hormuz.
2. The Strait handles about 80-85% of India's LPG imports and about 60% of its LNG imports.
3. Every $1 per barrel increase in oil prices adds about $1.8-2 billion to India's annual import bill.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. About 10 million Indians live and work in the Gulf. The conflict paralysed the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India's response to the West Asia conflict, consider the following statements:
1. India stopped all diplomatic engagement with West Asia leaders.
2. Seven inter-ministerial empowered groups were set up as rapid-response teams.
3. An economic stabilisation fund of Rs 573 billion was proposed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Prime Minister engaged directly with leadership across West Asia. India also diversified fertiliser sourcing to Russia, Morocco, Australia, Canada, Indonesia and Egypt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Strait of Hormuz, consider the following statements:
1. It lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
2. Fujairah Port, in the UAE, lies inside the Persian Gulf, beyond the Strait.
3. The IEA estimates about 15 million barrels a day of crude oil, around 34% of global crude trade, pass through it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Fujairah lies just outside the Strait on the Gulf of Oman, which lets the UAE bypass the Strait for oil exports. The Strait handles about a fifth of global liquid petroleum consumption and LNG trade.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to places affected by the conflict, consider the following statements:
1. Kharg Island is the export hub for about 90% of Iranian crude.
2. South Pars is the world's largest gas field, shared by Iran and Qatar.
3. Al Udeid in Qatar is the largest US base in the Middle East.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The US Fifth Fleet headquarters is at Juffair in Manama, Bahrain, and Natanz, Fordow and Isfahan are Iranian nuclear sites.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Red Sea is connected to the Gulf of Aden through which one of the following?
opts: Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf
questions.why: It connects to the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal. The Red Sea carries about 12% of world trade.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India's energy security, consider the following statements:
1. India imports over 85% of its crude oil and around 50% of its natural gas.
2. India's crude oil suppliers rose from 27 countries in 2006-07 to around 40 countries.
3. Phase II of the Strategic Petroleum Reserves programme includes Chandikhol in Odisha and Padur in Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India's primary energy consumption is expected to rise from about 775 Mtoe in 2013 to about 1,250 Mtoe in 2030.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India's foreign policy initiatives for energy security, consider the following statements:
1. HPCL signed a 10-year LNG agreement with ADNOC of the UAE.
2. Indian PSUs have 48 assets in 22 countries.
3. The Mercantile Marine Domain Awareness Centre monitors ships at chokepoints round the clock.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India also leads the Global Biofuel Alliance with the G20 and the International Solar Alliance.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Afghanistan-Pakistan conflict, consider the following statements:
1. The Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan emerged in 2007.
2. Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab Lil-Haq and Afghanistan launched Radd al-Zulm.
3. Qatar and Turkey brokered a lasting peace that ended the conflict.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Qatar and Turkey brokered only a temporary peace, and later talks mediated by Saudi Arabia dissolved toward the end of 2025. India condemned Pakistan's air strikes in Afghanistan.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Durand Line, consider the following statements:
1. Pakistan regards it as an unrecognised line.
2. It is a boundary of about 2,600 km drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan.
3. Afghanistan regards it as an imposed colonial demarcation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Pakistan recognises it as its sovereign boundary. Afghanistan has also raised Pashtun nationalism claims linking Pashtun tribes across the border.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Afghan-India Friendship Dam is the name of which one of the following?
questions.why: India maintains it as a humanitarian and infrastructure project. India can also resume the India-Afghan Air Freight Corridor and the Chabahar project.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the visit of the Prime Minister of Canada to India, consider the following statements:
1. Terms of Reference for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement were signed to raise trade to $50 billion by 2030.
2. A uranium supply deal of about $2.6 billion with Cameco covers 2027-2035.
3. Canada will join the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India supports Canada's entry into IORA as a Dialogue Partner, and an India-Canada Defence Dialogue is set up.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the uranium deal with Canada, consider the following statements:
1. India imports about 70% of its uranium because domestic ore is low grade.
2. The deal falls under the India-Canada Civil Nuclear Cooperation Agreement of 2010.
3. Reactors using imported uranium are under IAEA safeguards.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Indian ore is 0.02-0.45% concentration, while Canadian ore is 10-100 times richer. India's target is 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Canada relations, consider the following statements:
1. Relations were upgraded to a Strategic Partnership in 2018.
2. Bilateral trade was about USD 8.66 billion in 2024-25.
3. Canada is the world's largest producer of potash.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Irritants include Khalistan extremism and the 2023 Nijjar issue, and about 1.8 million Indo-Canadians live in Canada.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to para-diplomacy in India, consider the following statements:
1. It allows sub-national units to engage with foreign countries for their own interests.
2. Foreign affairs fall under the State List, so States have a free hand.
3. The MEA created a States Division in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Foreign affairs fall under Item 10 of the Union List, and States must not exceed their powers. Examples include Tamil Nadu's sensitivity on Sri Lanka and West Bengal's on Bangladesh.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Panama Canal and the Trincomalee project, consider the following statements:
1. The Panama Canal is about 82 km long and has been operational since 1914.
2. Trincomalee is a natural harbour on the north-eastern coast of Sri Lanka.
3. The Trincomalee Oil Tank Farm was built by the Japanese in the 1930s.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was built by the British in the 1930s to supply fuel to the Navy during the Second World War. India and Sri Lanka signed an agreement in 2022 for its joint development.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the India-Japan Bilateral Swap Arrangement, consider the following statements:
1. It was renewed with effect from 28 February 2026.
2. Its size remains unchanged at USD 75 billion.
3. It lets the two authorities swap local currencies for the US dollar.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Other currency swap arrangements include the SAARC CSA (2024-27), India-UAE and India-Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to IOS SAGAR and the Raisina Dialogue, consider the following statements:
1. The Raisina Dialogue is organised by NITI Aayog.
2. IOS SAGAR lets naval personnel of friendly countries train and sail on an Indian naval ship.
3. The 11th Raisina Dialogue had the theme 'Saṁskāra – Assertion, Accommodation, Advancement'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is organised by the Observer Research Foundation with the Ministry of External Affairs and has been held in New Delhi since 2016. The Raisina Science Diplomacy Initiative was launched.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA), consider the following statements:
1. It aims to develop 100 plug-and-play industrial parks of 100 to 1,000 acres.
2. It is implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
3. It has an outlay of Rs 33,660 crore from 2026-27 to 2031-32.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a scheme of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, implemented by the NICDC under the DPIIT. Support is up to Rs 1 crore per acre, and up to Rs 50 lakh per acre or 50% of infrastructure cost where private developers are involved.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the implementation of BHAVYA, consider the following statements:
1. The State or a Central PSU is the sponsoring agency.
2. A Special Purpose Vehicle between the NICDIT and the State nodal agency develops each park.
3. The SPV does not own the assets created under the scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The SPV owns the assets and is responsible for planning, construction, operation and maintenance. The parks use underground utility corridors and are aligned with PM GatiShakti.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) in India, consider the following statements:
1. India has signed MoUs with 24 countries on India Stack and DPI as of February 2026.
2. UPI is live in countries including the UAE, Singapore, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius and Qatar.
3. India placed DPI at the centre of the development agenda during its G20 Presidency in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. More than 25 nations are adopting or exploring the Modular Open-Source Identity Platform (MOSIP).

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Digital Public Goods (DPGs) and DPI, consider the following statements:
1. Bhashini is an example of a DPG, an AI-led language translation platform.
2. DPGs are open-source software, open standards, open data, open AI systems and open content.
3. DPGs are the broad digital infrastructures themselves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: DPGs often act as modular building blocks to operationalise DPI, but they are not the broad digital infrastructures themselves. India's DPI emerged through the JAM (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile) trinity.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The JAM Trinity in India's DPI refers to which one of the following?
opts: Jan Dhan, Atal Pension and Mudra
questions.why: It links identity, finance and connectivity at scale. India's DPI also follows a co-creation model with the private sector.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Fiscal Health Index (FHI) 2026 of NITI Aayog, consider the following statements:
1. It is the second annual edition of the Index.
2. The first edition covered both major States and the NE States.
3. It covers 18 major States and 10 North Eastern and Himalayan States for FY 2023-24 using CAG data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: FHI 2025 focused only on the 18 major States. States account for nearly one-third of India's general government debt.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the pillars and classification of the Fiscal Health Index, consider the following statements:
1. Quality of Expenditure, Revenue Mobilization, Fiscal Prudence, Debt Index and Debt Sustainability are its five pillars.
2. States are classified as Achiever, Front Runner, Performer and Aspirational.
3. The NE and Himalayan States were classified into four groups including Front Runner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The NE and Himalayan States were ranked separately and classified into 3 groups, with no Front Runner category.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the performance of States in the Fiscal Health Index 2026, consider the following:
1. Odisha is the top Achiever among the major States.
2. Gujarat is the top Front Runner among the major States.
3. Kerala is the first among the Aspirational major States.
4. Arunachal Pradesh is the top Achiever among NE and Himalayan States.
How many of the above of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: All four are correct. Nagaland is the first among the Aspirational NE and Himalayan States, and Tripura is the first Performer.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the semiconductor facility at Sanand, Gujarat, consider the following statements:
1. India currently meets about 60% of its semiconductor demand domestically.
2. It is India's first semiconductor assembly, test, marking and packaging (ATMP) facility.
3. It is operated by Micron Technology and has started India's first commercial chip production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India meets only about 10% of its semiconductor demand domestically. The market was valued at $52 billion in 2024-25 and is set to reach $100-110 billion by 2030.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), consider the following statements:
1. ISM 2.0 was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.
2. ISM includes a Design Linked Incentive Scheme and a Display Fabs Scheme.
3. Taiwan accounts for over 60% of global semiconductor manufacturing.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Taiwan also accounts for nearly 90% of the most advanced chips. The Digital India RISC-V Programme led to processors like SHAKTI and VIKRAM.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Regional Connectivity Scheme - Modified UDAN, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved for a 10-year period from 2026-27 to 2035-36 with an outlay of Rs 28,840 crore.
2. It plans to develop 100 airports from existing unserved airstrips over eight years.
3. It plans 200 modern helipads in hilly, remote, island and aspirational regions at Rs 15 crore each.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The airports are to be developed in 'Challenge Mode', and Viability Gap Funding to airlines runs for 10 years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the original UDAN scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched on 21 October 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy 2016.
2. It is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Civil Aviation implemented by the Airports Authority of India.
3. Of 925 awarded routes, 327 were discontinued.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It operationalised 663 routes across 95 airports and disbursed Rs 4,593.28 crore as VGF, and India's airports grew from 74 in 2014 to 159 in 2024.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to sector-specific UDAN initiatives, consider the following statements:
1. Krishi UDAN helps air transport of perishable agricultural produce.
2. UDAN 2.0 covered hilly and island territories.
3. UDAN 3.0 covered tourism routes and seaplanes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: UDAN 2.0 covered helipads and UDAN 4.0 covered hilly and island territories. UDAN Yatri Cafes offer affordable food at 17 airports.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the issues in civil aviation in India highlighted by a Parliamentary Standing Committee, consider the following statements:
1. The DGCA has a vacancy rate of 48.3%, with 843 incumbents against 1,630 sanctioned posts.
2. Recurring technical defects were found in 377 of 754 audited aircraft.
3. India already has a comprehensive statutory passenger rights framework.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India lacks a comprehensive statutory passenger rights framework despite carrying over 350 million passengers annually. The Committee suggests a Passenger Rights Charter under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Microfinance Institutions 2.0 (CGSMFI-2.0), consider the following statements:
1. An NBFC-MFI must deploy at least 25% of its total assets in microfinance loans.
2. It has a corpus of Rs 20,000 crore.
3. It is managed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company, owned by the Department of Financial Services.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: An NBFC-MFI is a non-deposit taking NBFC with at least 75% of total assets in microfinance loans, which are collateral-free loans to households with annual income up to Rs 3 lakh. Women are 95% of borrowers in microfinance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the modified Mutual Credit Guarantee Scheme for MSMEs, consider the following statements:
1. It gives a 60% credit guarantee through the NCGTC for loans up to Rs 100 crore.
2. The equipment cost threshold was raised from 60% to 75% of project cost.
3. Service sector MSMEs are now eligible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The threshold was reduced to 60% of the total project cost from 75%. The guarantee cover now expires after 10 years, and special provisions are included for exporters.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the new GDP series released by MoSPI, consider the following statements:
1. The new base year is 2022-23, replacing 2011-12.
2. Double deflation is now applied in manufacturing and agriculture.
3. The new series does not use GST or e-Vahan data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The new series integrates high-frequency and administrative data such as GST collections, the e-Vahan portal and PFMS. FY 2022-23 was chosen as the most recent normal period after Covid.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to other features of the new GDP series, consider the following statements:
1. Supply and Use Tables are aligned with national accounts.
2. The government accounts reflect the rollout of the National Pension System alongside the Old Pension Scheme.
3. The ASUSE and PLFS are used to measure the household and informal sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Hired domestic workers and platform and gig activities are also captured.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Flexible Inflation Targeting framework, consider the following statements:
1. It was recommended by an Expert Committee headed by Dr Urjit Patel.
2. Section 45ZA of the RBI Act, 1934 requires the Centre to set the inflation target every five years in consultation with the RBI.
3. The target of 4% with a band of 2% to 6% has been retained for 2026-2031.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Inflation outside the band for three consecutive quarters is a failure of the framework.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), consider the following statements:
1. All six members are appointed by the Central Government.
2. It has six members.
3. The RBI Governor is the ex-officio Chairperson.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The members are the Governor, the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board, and three external members appointed by the Centre.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Index of Core Industries, consider the following statements:
1. It covers coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement and electricity.
2. It is released by the National Statistical Office.
3. The eight core industries have about 40.27% weight in the Index of Industrial Production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade. Core growth slowed to 2.3% in February from 4.7% in January.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) is conducted by which one of the following?
questions.why: It covers the unincorporated non-agricultural sector and gives inputs for GDP estimates and national accounts.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the FDI policy for countries sharing a land border with India, consider the following statements:
1. A non-controlling investor from such countries owning less than 10% can invest under the Automatic Route.
2. Proposals in select sectors like electronics and capital goods are to be cleared within 60 days.
3. Press Note 3 of 2020 permitted such investments only under the Government route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In expedited cases, majority ownership and control must stay with resident Indian citizens or Indian-owned entities, and the beneficial owner is defined under the PMLA Rules, 2005.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Natural Gas (Supply Regulation) Order, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
2. It sets a four-tier priority allocation based on average gas use over the past six months.
3. Gas supply to power plants and petrochemical plants is guaranteed first.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Supplies are curtailed partly or fully for non-priority industries such as power plants and petrochemical facilities. Gas diverted to priority sectors is sold at a pooled price.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs), consider the following statements:
1. Their capacity is 5.33 million metric tonnes, enough for about 9.5 days of crude supplies.
2. They are managed by Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited, set up in 2004.
3. Phase-I facilities are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Phase-II, approved in 2021 with 6.5 MMT, is planned at Chandikhol in Odisha and Padur. The IEA benchmark is 90 days.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to natural gas and biogas in India, consider the following statements:
1. India aims to raise the share of natural gas in its energy mix to 15% by 2030.
2. Natural gas is mainly methane, and the share was 6.2% in 2025.
3. Biogas contains about 55-60% methane.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. GOBARdhan was launched in 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), and biogas yields bio-slurry that can be used as organic fertiliser.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the RELIEF scheme under the Export Promotion Mission, consider the following statements:
1. ECGC Ltd. is its nodal and implementing agency.
2. It helps exporters hit by freight escalation and war-related risks in the West Asia corridor.
3. It offers partial reimbursement of up to 50% to eligible non-ECGC-insured MSME exporters.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. ECGC was set up in 1957 to give credit risk insurance for exports.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the RoDTEP scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It is administered by the Ministry of Commerce.
2. It was launched in 2021 and replaced the MEIS.
3. It refunds taxes and levies on exported goods that are not otherwise reimbursed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is administered by the Department of Revenue under the Ministry of Finance. The MEIS was replaced after the WTO found it not in line with international trade practice.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the National Shipping Board and InvITs, consider the following statements:
1. The National Shipping Board is a statutory body established in 1959 under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958.
2. InvITs are regulated by the RBI.
3. Six of its members are elected by Parliament, four from the Lok Sabha and two from the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: InvITs are regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014. NHAI's first public InvIT was listed on the BSE.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), consider the following statements:
1. It began as the Indian Standards Institution in 1947.
2. The BIS Act, 2016 enables mandatory certification and hallmarking.
3. Its headquarters is at Mumbai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Its headquarters is in New Delhi, with five regional offices at Kolkata, Chennai, Mumbai, Chandigarh and Delhi. Over 23,300 Indian standards are in force.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to coconut cultivation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Coconut needs very low rainfall of below 500 mm.
2. India is the world's largest producer, with nearly 30% of global production.
3. Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka are the major producers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Coconut needs 1,000-2,500 mm of annual rainfall, 20-32 degrees Celsius, and well-drained sandy loam, laterite or coastal alluvial soils. Budget 2026-27 announced a Coconut Promotion Scheme.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the role of MSMEs in defence, consider the following statements:
1. The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated an all-time high Rs 7.85 lakh crore to the Ministry of Defence.
2. iDEX and the Technology Development Fund are among the schemes for them.
3. ideaForge supplies UAVs for high-altitude transport and border surveillance to the Indian Army.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. EyeROV and Sagar Defence Engineering build underwater and surface drones, and Qnu Labs, QpiAI and Signalchip work on quantum-secure communications.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to SIPRI's Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025, consider the following statements:
1. India was the second largest recipient of major arms in 2021-25, accounting for 8.2% of global imports.
2. India's top supplier in 2021-25 was France with 40% share.
3. India's overall arms imports fell by 4.0% between 2016-20 and 2021-25.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Russia was the top supplier with 40%, followed by France at 29% and Israel at 15%. Ukraine was the largest importer.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Global Terrorism Index 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is published by the Institute for Economics and Peace, a Sydney-based think tank.
2. Pakistan recorded the highest score as the country most affected by terrorism.
3. Deaths from terrorism rose by 28% in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Deaths from terrorism fell by 28% and attacks fell by about 22%. About 70% of deaths occurred in five countries, and India ranked 13th.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to recent defence contracts and weapons, consider the following statements:
1. The Minuteman III is a US submarine-launched ballistic missile.
2. Six ALH Mk-III (Maritime Role) helicopters are being acquired from HAL for the Indian Coast Guard.
3. The Vertical Launch Shtil is a surface-to-air missile contracted with the Russian Rosoboronexport.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Minuteman III is a land-based intercontinental ballistic missile under the US Air Force Global Strike Command. A gravity bomb has no engine, unlike a cruise missile.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Exercise LAMITIYE-2026 is a biennial joint military exercise between India and which one of the following?
questions.why: The 2026 edition was the first with tri-services participation from India. Sea Dragon 2026 is a US Navy-led anti-submarine warfare exercise.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the draft amendment of the EIA Notification, 2006, consider the following statements:
1. A Standing Authority on EIA in each State can take over the functions of SEIAA for a maximum of 1 year if it is non-functional.
2. A Standing Committee can perform the SEAC's duties for a maximum of 1 year.
3. If a SEAC fails to complete appraisal within 120 days, the proposal moves to the Standing Committee through the Parivesh portal.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The draft was published under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to reduce delays at State level, where the tenure of State bodies is 3 years.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the EIA process in India, consider the following statements:
1. Category A projects need prior environmental clearance from the Centre on the recommendation of an Expert Appraisal Committee.
2. Category B2 projects are required to undergo a full EIA.
3. Category B projects need clearance from the SEIAA on the recommendation of a SEAC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Category B2 projects are exempt from EIA. Solar and wind projects and hydro projects below 25 MW are also exempt.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to judgments related to EIA, consider the following statements:
1. Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum recognised the polluter pays and the precautionary principles.
2. Centre for Environmental Law v. Union of India (2018) stressed stakeholder inputs through public consultation.
3. Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India rejected the role of EIA in decision-making.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court upheld the role of EIA in balancing development and environmental protection. India has not ratified the Espoo Convention, 1991 on EIA in a Transboundary Context.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution for 2031-35, consider the following statements:
1. The new target is a 47% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP from 2005 levels by 2035.
2. The new target is 60% of installed electric capacity from non-fossil sources by 2035.
3. The new carbon sink target is 3.5-4 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2035.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India's non-fossil share of installed capacity was 52.57% by February 2026, and the first NDC was submitted in 2015 and updated in 2022.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's climate policy instruments, consider the following statements:
1. The MISHTI scheme is for restoration of coral reefs.
2. The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was notified in 2023 under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.
3. Obligated sectors include petroleum refinery, cement, aluminium, textiles and pulp and paper.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: MISHTI is for mangrove restoration. The National Action Plan on Climate Change works alongside State Action Plans.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to challenges in achieving India's NDC, consider the following statements:
1. Non-fossil sources account for more than 50% of installed capacity but less than 30% of electricity generated.
2. Coal still accounts for about 55% of electricity generation.
3. NITI Aayog estimates energy transition investment of about USD 250 billion per year till 2047.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Other challenges include the cost of battery storage and dependence on imported critical minerals like lithium.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted at COP 15 of the CBD in 2022 and replaced the Aichi targets.
2. It is a legally binding treaty.
3. It has 23 targets for 2030 including the 30 by 30 target.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is non-binding. Its financial mechanism is the Global Biodiversity Framework Fund managed by the GEF, with 20% earmarked for indigenous peoples.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the financing targets of the Kunming-Montreal framework, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to mobilise at least $200 billion per year.
2. Developed countries are to give developing countries at least $20 billion a year by 2025 and $30 billion by 2030.
3. It targets halving the introduction of invasive species.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also targets reducing harmful subsidies by $500 billion a year and halving risks from pesticides and hazardous chemicals.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's 7th National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity, consider the following statements:
1. It was submitted under Article 26 of the CBD.
2. It tracks 23 national biodiversity targets under the NBSAP 2024-30.
3. It shows forest and tree cover at 25.17% of the geographical area.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Recorded forest area is 23.59%, and 24.1 million hectares are restored or under restoration against the Bonn Challenge pledge of 26 million hectares.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the wildlife figures in India's 7th National Report to the CBD, consider the following:
1. 98 Ramsar sites as of 2026
2. 3,682 tigers
3. 718 snow leopards
4. 6,327 riverine dolphins
How many of the above of the above are figures given in the report?
questions.why: All four are given in the report. India ranks 1st in Asia and 3rd globally for Ramsar sites, and has 22,446 elephants and 891 Asiatic lions.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the protected area network of India as given in the report, consider the following statements:
1. Protected areas cover 5.71% of the land area.
2. India has 58 Tiger Reserves and 18 Biosphere Reserves.
3. India has 574 Wildlife Sanctuaries and 106 National Parks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. There are also 390 Community Reserves and 145 Conservation Reserves, and about 29.77% of India's area is under land degradation.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit Sharing, consider the following statements:
1. It is a supplementary agreement under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
2. It was adopted in 2010 and entered into force in 2014.
3. It requires Prior Informed Consent from the provider and benefit sharing on Mutually Agreed Terms.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India implements it through the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, with the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's first National Report on the Nagoya Protocol, consider the following statements:
1. India issued 12,830 ABS approvals.
2. India published 3,556 Internationally Recognised Certificates of Compliance, about 60% of the global share.
3. India has set up fewer than 10,000 Biodiversity Management Committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India has established over 2.76 lakh BMCs. Rs 216.31 crore was mobilised, of which Rs 139.69 crore was distributed to communities, farmers and BMCs.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the International Solar Alliance (ISA), consider the following statements:
1. It celebrated its 10th Foundation Day on 11 March 2026.
2. The Indian Prime Minister described it as an 'alternative OPEC'.
3. It helps Least Developed Countries and Small Island Developing States by aggregating demand.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. ISA contributes to SDG 7 and SDG 13, and challenges include funding, high tariffs on solar PV and storage costs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the 2025 Dharali flash flood in Uttarakhand, consider the following statements:
1. It was a GLOF from a moraine-dammed lake.
2. An ISRO study found it was caused by the collapse of an exposed ice patch in the nivation zone of Srikanta Glacier.
3. It was not a cloudburst or a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The study links the collapse to deglaciation and calls exposed ice patches an under-recognised risk. Nivation is erosion beneath and around a snow bank due to alternate freezing and thawing.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the ICIMOD report on glacier melting in the Hindu Kush Himalaya, consider the following statements:
1. The rate of glacier melting has doubled since 2000.
2. The Karakoram remained relatively stable with about 2% loss.
3. The Ganga and Brahmaputra basins lost 21% and 16% of glacier area, respectively.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The region lost 12% of glacier area and 9% of ice reserves between 1990 and 2020, and glaciers smaller than 0.5 sq km shrink the fastest.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme, consider the following statements:
1. It is an NDMA initiative with Phase-1 from 2023 to 2026.
2. It targets Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, J&K and Ladakh.
3. The nodal bodies for glacier studies and GLOF hazards are the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Central Water Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Chamoli 2021, Sikkim 2023 and Dharali 2025 are cited as cascading disasters.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme, consider the following statements:
1. Projects of 25 MW or below are classified as small hydro.
2. Small hydro is looked after by the Ministry of Power.
3. The scheme runs from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs 2,584.60 crore for about 1,500 MW.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is looked after by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. The estimated potential is 21,133 MW from 7,133 sites, and about half is in hilly States.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Under the classification of hydropower by capacity, a 1.5 MW project is categorised as which one of the following?
questions.why: Micro is up to 100 kW, mini is 101 kW to 2 MW and small hydro is 2 MW to 25 MW.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to reports released on the environment, consider the following statements:
1. The State of the World's Migratory Species interim report 2026 was published by the CMS secretariat.
2. About 49% of CMS-listed migratory species show declining populations.
3. The UN World Water Development Report 2026 has the theme 'Water and Gender'.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. About 24% of CMS-protected species are globally threatened, and 2.1 billion people lack safely managed drinking water.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the SDG Bulletin released by MoSPI, consider the following statements:
1. Electrification coverage rose from 99.77% to 100%.
2. The share of renewables in installed capacity rose from 16.02% to 22.13% between 2015-16 and 2024-25.
3. Door-to-door waste collection fell from 97.7% to 43%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Door-to-door waste collection rose from 43% to 97.7%, and waste processing reached 80.7%. India is the fourth-largest wind energy producer.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the WMO report 'State of the Global Climate 2025', consider the following statements:
1. Earth's energy imbalance reached a 65-year peak.
2. 2025 was about 1.43 degrees Celsius above the 1850-1900 average.
3. 2015 to 2025 are the hottest 11 years on record.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Earth's energy imbalance is the difference between incoming solar energy and outgoing long-wave radiation, and the report was released on World Meteorological Day, 23 March.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the NH Green Cover Index and the National Productivity Council, consider the following statements:
1. The NPC was set up in 1958 and falls under the Ministry of Environment.
2. The NH-Green Cover Index was released by NHAI with the National Remote Sensing Centre of ISRO.
3. The NPC is to act as the Environment Audit Designated Agency under the Environment Audit Rules, 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The NPC is an autonomous organisation under the DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. India is a founding member of the Tokyo-based Asian Productivity Organisation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the M.C. Mehta case and other landmark environmental cases, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court recognised the principle of absolute liability in the M.C. Mehta case.
2. In S.P. Muthuraman (2025) the Court upheld post-facto environmental clearances.
3. T.N. Godavarman (1995) expanded the definition of forest to include all areas recorded as forest in government records.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: In S.P. Muthuraman (2025) the Court declared post-facto or retrospective environmental clearances illegal. The M.C. Mehta PIL of 1985 was formally disposed of.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC), consider the following statements:
1. India is setting up a first-of-its-kind OTEC plant at Kavaratti in Lakshadweep.
2. It generates electricity from the temperature difference between warm surface water and cold deep water.
3. It needs a temperature difference of about 2 degrees Celsius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It needs about 20 degrees Celsius of difference and is viable in tropical oceans between 30 degrees N and S. It can provide round-the-clock power and desalination.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: 'Dark oxygen' discovered in the deep Pacific Ocean is produced by which one of the following?
opts: Volcanic release of oxygen gas at vents
Bacterial breakdown of methane at seeps
questions.why: It is produced without sunlight at nearly 4,000 m depth. It challenges the belief that photosynthesis is the only major natural source of oxygen.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to India-China border trade, consider the following statements:
1. Trade through Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh was to commence from 1 June.
2. In 2025 the two sides agreed to reopen trade through Lipulekh, Shipki La and Nathu La.
3. The Sutlej River enters India at Shipki La.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Shipki La was earlier known as Pema La, or Shared Pass, and trade was disrupted by Doklam and the Covid pandemic.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to Rossby waves and wet-bulb temperature, consider the following statements:
1. Rossby waves are large undulating movements of the atmosphere moving westward.
2. Stalled Rossby waves can trap hot, humid air and cause heatwaves.
3. A wet-bulb temperature above 31.5 degrees Celsius is considered harmful as the body cannot cool by sweating.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Rising sea surface temperatures were linked to a 50-64% rise in humid heatwaves over land.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's judgment in Harish Rana v. Union of India (2026), consider the following statements:
1. It required a fresh 30-day consideration period in all cases without exception.
2. The Court for the first time permitted withdrawal of life-supporting care for a man in a vegetative state for 13 years.
3. It held that Clinically Assisted Nutrition and Hydration is a medical treatment that may be withdrawn if it serves no therapeutic purpose.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court waived the usual 30-day period as parents and medical boards unanimously agreed recovery was impossible. The judgment is governed by the best interests of the patient principle.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the legal position on euthanasia in India, consider the following statements:
1. Active euthanasia is illegal in India.
2. In Aruna Shanbaug (2011) the Court rejected passive euthanasia in all circumstances.
3. In Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab (1996) the Court held that the right to life does not include the right to die.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court rejected the plea in the case but allowed passive euthanasia under strict conditions for terminal and irreversible patients. In Common Cause (2018) it recognised the right to die with dignity under Article 21 and the concept of a living will.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: A 'living will' recognised by the Supreme Court in the Common Cause case (2018) is which one of the following?
opts: A will bequeathing property to a caregiver
A court order appointing a guardian
A hospital policy on organ donation
questions.why: It is used if the person becomes incompetent or unable to communicate. The 2023 guidelines modified the procedure, involving medical boards and judicial officers.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It amends the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
2. The District Magistrate issues the certificate after examining the recommendation of a designated medical board.
3. It retains the legal recognition of self-perceived gender identity under Section 4(2) of the 2019 Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It omits Section 4(2) of the 2019 Act, removing the recognition of self-determination, and the definition excludes self-perceived gender identities. The medical board is headed by a Chief Medical Officer or Deputy CMO.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the other provisions of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The National Council for Transgender Persons will have rotational representation of States and UTs, one each from the North, South, East, West and North-East.
2. Kidnapping or causing grievous hurt to force a person to assume a transgender identity is an offence.
3. Forcing a person to present as transgender for begging or bonded labour is punishable.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Representatives must have a minimum rank of Director, and critics say the Act effectively excludes trans-men and non-binary persons.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the status of transgender persons in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Yogyakarta Principles recommend recognising gender through medical procedures.
2. The 2011 Census estimated 4.8 lakh transgender persons.
3. Their literacy rate was reported at 56.1% against the national 74.04% (Census 2011).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Yogyakarta Principles call for gender recognition based on self-identification without mandating any medical procedure. About 96% face discrimination in employment as per NHRC (2018).

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA), consider the following statements:
1. It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
2. It was established in 1990 and given statutory status under the JJ Act, 2015.
3. It is the Central Authority for inter-country adoption under the Hague Convention of 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India ratified the Hague Convention on Inter-country Adoption in 2003, and SARAs, CWCs and DCPUs work at the State and local levels.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the legal framework for adoption in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956 permits adoption by Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs.
2. Parents adopting under HAMA must register the deed with CARA.
3. The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 governs guardianship for Muslims and Christians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Parents adopting under HAMA are not required to register the adoption deed with CARA. The JJ Act, 2015 provides an adoption framework open to everyone.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the CARINGS portal and recent directions of CARA, consider the following statements:
1. CARINGS is maintained by CARA and was developed by the National Informatics Centre.
2. A two-month reconsideration period must be followed for surrendered children before they are declared legally free for adoption.
3. CARINGS is separate from the Mission Vatsalya portal and has no integration with it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: CARINGS has been integrated with the unified Mission Vatsalya portal. Section 74 of the JJ Act, 2015 prohibits disclosing the identity of children in conflict with law or in need of care.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to maternity benefit for adoptive mothers, consider the following statements:
1. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 reduced paid maternity leave for biological mothers to 12 weeks.
2. The Supreme Court held Section 60(4) of the Social Security Code, 2020 unconstitutional.
3. The provision allowed maternity benefit only if the adopted child was under 3 months of age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 2017 Act extended paid maternity leave for biological mothers to 26 weeks. The Court said adoption is an exercise of reproductive and decisional autonomy under Article 21.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to AI in education in India, consider the following statements:
1. NEP 2020 acknowledges the role of AI, big data and machine learning.
2. SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness) builds AI skills for students of classes 6-12 and educators.
3. SWAYAM offers free AI courses from the IITs and IISc.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The UGC's 2022 undergraduate curriculum also includes AI, big data analysis and machine learning.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the IMPAct4Nutrition (I4N) platform, consider the following statements:
1. NITI Aayog and UNICEF India signed a Statement of Intent through the platform for aspirational districts and blocks.
2. It connects businesses with the social movement around POSHAN 2.0.
3. The ACE Card initiative stands for Assets, CSR and Employees engagement for nutrition.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The I4N serves as a hub of knowledge and resources on nutrition.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to data centres in India, consider the following statements:
1. Data centre capacity rose from about 375 MW in 2020 to about 1,500 MW by 2025.
2. The Budget 2026-27 gives a tax holiday till 2047 to eligible foreign companies providing cloud services from India.
3. Data centres with an IT load above 5 MW got infrastructure status in 2022.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Budget also gives a 15% safe harbour on cost where the Indian data centre is a related entity of a foreign company.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to challenges for data centres in India, consider the following statements:
1. Cooling a 100 MW hyperscale facility can consume up to 2 million litres of water a day.
2. Data centre electricity demand is projected to nearly halve by 2030.
3. Over 70% of operational capacity is concentrated in Mumbai, Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The IEA projects that electricity demand from data centres will nearly double by 2030. Alternatives such as immersion and direct-to-chip cooling can cut water and power use.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to NavIC (IRNSS), consider the following statements:
1. It is an independent regional navigation satellite system developed by ISRO.
2. Its service area extends about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass.
3. At least 4 satellites with working atomic clocks are required for the system to function.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. After the last atomic clock on IRNSS-1F stopped, only three satellites (IRNSS-1B, 1I and NVS-01) can provide PNT services, and 6 of 11 satellites have failed due to atomic clocks.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the NavIC satellite constellation, consider the following statements:
1. IRNSS-1A, launched in 2013, was India's first dedicated navigation satellite.
2. NVS-01, launched on GSLV-F12 in 2023, carried an indigenous atomic clock for the first time.
3. NVS-02, launched on GSLV-F15 in 2025, reached its designated orbit successfully.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: NVS-02 failed to reach its designated orbit. The NVS series adds L1 band signals to the earlier L5 and S bands.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the services of NavIC, consider the following statements:
1. The Standard Positioning Service gives a position accuracy of worse than 100 metres.
2. The Standard Positioning Service is available for all civilian users.
3. The Restricted Service is an encrypted service for authorised users.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: SPS gives position accuracy better than 20 metres and timing accuracy better than 40 nanoseconds. SPS signals are interoperable with GPS, Glonass, Galileo and BeiDou.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: NavIC reduces India's reliance on the US-owned GPS.
Statement-II: The US denied the use of GPS to India during the Kargil War in 1999.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct. The denial of GPS in Kargil is cited to show the risk of reliance, and about 8,700 trains are equipped with NavIC.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the new particle Xi-cc-plus discovered at the Large Hadron Collider, consider the following statements:
1. It is made up of two charm quarks and one down quark.
2. It is lighter than a proton.
3. Its discovery was the 80th particle discovery at the LHC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Its mass is about four times heavier than a proton, since up quarks are replaced by charm quarks. It helps scientists understand the strong force.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to quarks and the strong force, consider the following statements:
1. Quarks come in six flavours: up, down, charm, strange, top and bottom.
2. Baryons such as protons and neutrons are made of three quarks.
3. Mesons are made of three quarks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Mesons such as pions and kaons are made of two quarks. The strong force is about 100 times stronger than electromagnetism but acts over very short distances.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to CERN and the Large Hadron Collider, consider the following statements:
1. India is a full member of CERN.
2. The LHC is a 27-km ring of superconducting magnets about 100 metres underground.
3. CERN was founded in 1954 and is situated at the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is an associate member. The LHC discovered the Higgs boson in 2012, and also exotic hadrons and toponium.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to food fortification in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Food Safety and Standards (Fortification of Food) Regulations, 2018 give standards for fortified foods.
2. The rice fortification scheme under PMGKAY was permanently expanded after an IIT Kharagpur study.
3. FSSAI has standards for fortifying rice, wheat flour, edible oil, milk and salt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The scheme was temporarily discontinued citing an IIT Kharagpur study on nutrient stability. Fortified Rice Kernels are mixed with regular rice at a 1:100 ratio.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the methods of food fortification, consider the following statements:
1. Bio-fortification enhances nutrients while crops are grown, for example the Vitamin A-rich orange sweet potato.
2. Industrial fortification adds micronutrients during processing, for example iodine in salt.
3. Home fortification is done only in factories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Home fortification is done by individuals adding items such as iron sprinkles or nutrient sachets to meals. Concerns include lower bioavailability and shelf-life degradation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It targets 14-year-old girls and is free of cost.
2. It requires mandatory parental consent.
3. It uses a single dose of Gardasil-4, given intramuscularly.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It was launched on 28 February 2026 and runs intensively for 90 days at designated government health facilities.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to HPV and its vaccines, consider the following statements:
1. Cervical cancer is the only cancer preventable by a vaccine, and the vaccine protects against all HPV types.
2. HPV types 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers globally and over 80% in India.
3. Cervavac is an indigenous quadrivalent vaccine made by the Serum Institute of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The vaccine protects against specific types, for example Gardasil-4 covers types 6, 11, 16 and 18. WHO's 90-70-90 targets are 90% girls vaccinated by 15, 70% women screened by 35 and 45, and 90% treated.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to digital tools and partners of the HPV campaign, consider the following statements:
1. U-WIN is used for registration of beneficiaries.
2. eVIN tracks vaccine stocks.
3. Gavi was formed in 2000 as a public-private partnership and supplies Gardasil doses for the campaign.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. A parliamentary committee in 2011 found no conclusive link between the 2009 PATH project and the girls' deaths, but trust was damaged.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the IndiaAI Mission as assessed by a Parliamentary Standing Committee, consider the following statements:
1. The Mission utilised only 32% of its Revised Estimate in 2025-26 as of December 2025.
2. AI research funding is spread widely across all colleges.
3. The Budget Estimate for 2026-27 was halved against proposed requirements.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Funding is largely restricted to premier institutions like IITs and national laboratories, which limits ecosystem growth. The Committee also flagged the power and water use of data centres.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Moonshot project on brain co-processors by IISc and the Pratiksha Trust, consider the following statements:
1. Brain co-processors are AI-powered bidirectional neural interfaces that decode, analyse and re-encode brain signals.
2. The primary goal is to restore reach and grasp in stroke survivors.
3. Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation and tDCS require electrodes placed on the bare brain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: TMS and tDCS are non-invasive and do not need electrodes on the bare brain. Unlike conventional BCIs, co-processors target the full cognitive loop.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Digital Twin initiative at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, consider the following statements:
1. It is the first port in India to launch a Digital Twin initiative.
2. The port is an artificial deep-sea harbour at Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu.
3. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system using real-time data.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Technologies include IoT sensors, GPS tracking, LiDAR mapping, drone imaging and CCTV networks, and Ptolemy described Tuticorin as a trade centre in 123 AD.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to V2X technology and the KAVACH system, consider the following statements:
1. KAVACH prevents only head-on collisions.
2. V2X lets vehicles communicate with other vehicles, pedestrians and roadside infrastructure.
3. KAVACH is a Train Collision Avoidance System developed by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: KAVACH prevents head-on, rear-end and side-on collisions and signal passing at danger. It also repeats signals in foggy weather and activates the horn automatically.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the GARBH-INi programme, consider the following statements:
1. It is supported by the Department of Biotechnology.
2. It is among the largest pregnancy cohorts in South Asia, established from 2015 at Gurugram Civil Hospital.
3. It aims to develop AI-driven solutions for preterm births.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It has set up a national biorepository and the GARBH-INi-DRISHTI data-sharing platform.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to set up 6,000 MTPA of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity.
2. The outlay of Rs 7,280 crore consists of a capital subsidy of Rs 6,450 crore and a sales-linked incentive of Rs 750 crore.
3. Five beneficiaries are to be selected through global competitive bidding, each up to 1,200 MTPA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The capital subsidy is Rs 750 crore and the sales-linked incentive is Rs 6,450 crore. The scheme is of the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the World Obesity Atlas 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was released by the World Obesity Federation.
2. Obesity among school-age children rose from 4% in 1975 to nearly 20% in 2022.
3. India ranks second globally for children who are overweight and living with obesity.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. About 41 million school-age children in India have a high BMI. BMI is weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in metres.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to GLP-1 drugs, consider the following statements:
1. They mimic the natural GLP-1 hormone and help regulate blood sugar and appetite.
2. Ozempic and Wegovy are examples.
3. The CDSCO has permitted their advertisement to the public.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The CDSCO prohibited companies from advertising GLP-1 drugs amid concerns about misuse. They slow digestion and increase the feeling of fullness.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to white and brown fat, consider the following statements:
1. Brown fat is the most abundant fat in adults.
2. White fat stores energy in the form of triglycerides.
3. Brown fat burns energy and converts it into heat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: White fat is the most abundant, and it also releases leptin and adiponectin. Brown fat is found mainly in the neck and upper chest and is triggered by cold.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to antiprotons, consider the following statements:
1. They are antimatter particles with the same mass as a proton but a negative charge.
2. They were first produced by Emilio Segrè and Owen Chamberlain.
3. Scientists at CERN transported them by road for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The work helps address the matter-antimatter mystery, as the Big Bang should have produced equal amounts.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to megamasers and molecular clouds, consider the following statements:
1. The MeerKAT telescope in South Africa discovered the brightest and most distant megamaser.
2. Molecular clouds are transparent as they have no dust.
3. A megamaser emits microwaves amplified from excited hydroxyl molecules during galaxy mergers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Molecular clouds are opaque because of internal dust grains and have no clearly defined boundaries. Hydrogen (H2) is the most common molecule in them.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Dimethyl Ether (DME), consider the following statements:
1. CSIR-NCL has developed a DME production process technology.
2. DME can be blended with LPG up to 20%.
3. DME can be produced from coal, methanol or captured CO2.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. DME is a colourless gas with minimal SOx, NOx and particulate emissions and is seen as an alternative to LPG.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Mahad Satyagraha, consider the following statements:
1. It was led by Dr B.R. Ambedkar on 20 March 1927 to secure Dalits' right to use water from the Chawdar Tank.
2. It was organised by the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha founded in 1924.
3. It was led by Mahatma Gandhi at Mahad in 1927.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was led by Dr Ambedkar, though Gandhi wrote in Young India to support it. 20 March is observed as Social Empowerment Day, and the centenary runs through 2026-27.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the background of the Mahad Satyagraha, consider the following statements:
1. The Second Satyagraha of December 1927 went ahead despite a court injunction.
2. In 1923 the Bombay Legislative Council passed a resolution to grant untouchables access to state-funded public watering places.
3. In 1924 the Mahad Municipality opened the Chawdar Tank to untouchables, but this remained on paper.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Dr Ambedkar postponed the Second Satyagraha after a lawsuit claimed the tank was private property and secured an injunction. On 17 March 1937 the Bombay High Court declared the tank public property.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to movements against caste discrimination in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873.
2. The Harijan Sevak Sangh was established in 1932 by Dr Ambedkar.
3. The Self-Respect Movement was founded in 1925 by E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was established by Mahatma Gandhi in 1932. The Mahad Satyagraha prompted the Congress to reconstitute its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under Madan Mohan Malaviya.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The core objective of the Mahad Satyagraha is directly reflected in which one of the following Articles of the Constitution?
opts: Article 21, which protects the right to life
questions.why: The demand for equal access to public wells and tanks mirrors Article 15. Dr Ambedkar compared the Satyagraha to the French National Assembly of 1789.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Gyan Bharatam Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector scheme of the Ministry of Culture with an outlay of Rs 491.66 crore for 2025-2031.
